# Solve

> Solve (the `solve-engine` package on npm) evaluates the lines a person writes in a note: arithmetic, percentages, units, currencies, dates and times, statistics, finance and symbolic algebra, in plain phrasing, one line or a whole document at a time.

Each line of a note is worked out on its own unless it reads another: a name defined on one line (`price = 20`) is read by the lines below it, and forms such as `total above`, `line 3`, `#tag` totals, `check`, what-if (`with`) and `inputs of` work across lines. Text after `//` is a comment. Every example these files show is proven against the engine when the documentation is built.

## Writing a note

- [Labels](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/labels/): words that name a line's figure, kept as text while the rest is worked out, before a colon or, when an amount of money or a quantity ends the line, without one.

## Arithmetic

- [Operators](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/operators/): add, subtract, multiply, divide and raise to a power, in symbols or in words, with multiplication done before addition. `%` means percent, so the remainder after a division is `mod`.
- [Number suffixes](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/number-suffixes/): a letter after a number as shorthand for thousands (`k`), millions (`M`), billions (`B`) and trillions (`T`).
- [Decimals](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/decimals/): a number with a decimal point is kept as the exact decimal you typed and worked in base ten, so `0.1 + 0.2` is exactly 0.3 rather than a near miss.
- [Fractions](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/fractions/): a quotient of whole numbers stays exact, and `as fraction` shows it as one.
- [Percentages](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/percentages/): a percentage of a number, a discount or a markup, the change from one value to another, and the whole a percentage was taken from.
- [Ratios](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/ratios/): a ratio reduced to its lowest whole-number terms.
- [Rounding](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/rounding/): to a number of decimal places (dp), in a chosen direction, or to the nearest ten, hundred or other step.
- [Number functions](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/number-functions/): everyday maths functions such as the square root, the absolute value (the size of a number without its sign) and the greatest common divisor (the largest number that divides both).
- [Uncertainty](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/uncertainty/): a measurement with a tolerance, written `+/-`, carried through the arithmetic so the answer says how far it can be trusted.
- [Conditionals](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/conditionals/): comparisons that answer true or false, `and`, `or` and `not`, and `if ... then ... else`.

## Numbers

- [Numerals](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/numerals/): a number written out in words, as an ordinal (1st, 2nd, 3rd) or in Roman numerals.
- [Big integers](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/big-integers/): whole numbers past 9,007,199,254,740,991, where an ordinary floating-point number starts to drop digits, stay exact; the `n` suffix writes one directly.
- [Primes, factors and counting](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/number-theory/): testing whether a number is prime, breaking it into its prime factors, and factorials (`5!` is every whole number from 1 to 5 multiplied together).
- [Complex numbers](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/complex/): numbers with an imaginary part, written with `i` (the square root of -1), which is what the square root of a negative number needs.
- [Constants](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/constants/): named physical and mathematical constants, carrying their units.

## Programmer math

- [Number bases](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/number-bases/): numbers written in hexadecimal (`0x`), binary (`0b`) or octal (`0o`), and shown in any of them with `as`.
- [Bit shifting](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/bit-shifting/): moving the bits of a whole number left or right, which multiplies or divides it by a power of two.
- [Bitwise operators](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/bitwise-operators/): and, or, exclusive or (`xor`) and complement, applied to each bit of a whole number.
- [Data sizes](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/data-sizes/): bytes and bits, with the decimal prefixes (a kB is 1,000 bytes) kept apart from the binary ones (a KiB is 1,024), and how long a download takes at a given speed.

## Algebra

- [Expanding](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/expanding/): multiplying out brackets and collecting the like terms.
- [Factoring](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/factoring/): writing a polynomial as a product of simpler factors, the reverse of expanding.
- [Solving equations](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/solving-equations/): the values of an unknown that make an equation true, exactly where there is a method and numerically where there is not.
- [Cancelling a fraction](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/cancelling-fractions/): a fraction of polynomials reduced to its lowest terms.
- [Splitting a fraction](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/splitting-fractions/): a fraction of polynomials broken into the simpler fractions that add up to it (partial fractions).
- [Exact coefficients](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/exact-coefficients/): the numbers in front of the terms of a symbolic expression (its coefficients) stay exact fractions, so they pick up no floating-point error.
- [Calculus](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/calculus/): derivatives (rates of change), integrals (areas under a curve), limits, Taylor series and Jacobians.
- [Symbolic](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/symbolic/): a letter with no value stays an unknown rather than an error, and `=>` at the end of a line asks for the simplified expression.

## Statistics

- [Vectors & matrices](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/vectors-and-matrices/): lists of numbers in square brackets, with `;` between the rows of a matrix, worked on element by element or with linear algebra.
- [Map, reduce & aggregates](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/map-reduce-and-aggregates/): a range written `start:end`, an expression applied to every item of a list, and a list folded down to one value. A range is read only inside brackets or a function call, since a bare `0:3` is a clock time.
- [Statistics](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/statistics/): averages, medians, totals and other summaries of a list, in plain phrasing.
- [Probability distributions](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/probability-distributions/): the normal, binomial, Poisson and Student's t distributions, for the chance of a result and the result for a chance.

## Finance

- [Currency](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/currency/): money written with a symbol, a code or a word. Converting between currencies, as in `10 USD in GBP`, uses live exchange rates, so it has no fixed answer to show here.
- [Money precision](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/money-precision/): money is held as an exact decimal, so a column of prices adds up to the cent instead of drifting by a fraction of a penny.
- [Tax](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/tax/): adding tax to a price, taking it off a total, or finding how much of a total was tax.
- [Recurring schedules](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/recurring-schedules/): the total of a payment that repeats, such as rent every month for a year and a half.
- [Splitting a bill](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/splitting-a-bill/): an amount divided between people, with the odd penny accounted for rather than lost.
- [Interest & inflation](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/interest-and-inflation/): compound interest, loan and mortgage repayments, and what an amount of money from one year is worth in another.
- [Investments](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/investments/): what a sum grows to at a rate, what a future sum is worth today, and the return on what was invested.
- [Savings goals](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/savings-goals/): how long it takes to reach a target, or how much to put by each month.
- [NPV, IRR & payback](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/cash-flow/): judging an investment from its cash flows, the money paid out first and the money that comes back after: the net present value (NPV, what the flows are worth today) and the internal rate of return (IRR, the rate at which they break even).
- [Payroll & take-home](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/payroll/): UK take-home pay from a salary, after income tax and National Insurance.
- [Comparison shopping](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/shopping/): which of two prices is the better deal, and by how much, with `vs`.
- [Stocks](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/stocks/): share and coin prices, as in `stock(AAPL)` and `crypto("BTC")`, from a data source the host application supplies. A price is live, so there is no fixed answer to show here.
- [crypto](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/crypto/): share and coin prices, as in `stock(AAPL)` and `crypto("BTC")`, from a data source the host application supplies. A price is live, so there is no fixed answer to show here.

## Dates

- [Date literals](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/date-literals/): a date written day first, year first, or with the month's name.
- [Date arithmetic](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/date-arithmetic/): adding days, weeks, months or hours to a date, or taking them away.
- [Relative dates](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/relative-dates/): a day named by its relation to today, such as tomorrow, next friday, three days ago or the end of the month. Each keeps the time of day unless the app starts relative days at midnight.
- [Relative months](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/relative-months/): a month named by its relation to now, which gives the month's first day.
- [The nth weekday](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/nth-weekday/): the nth, or the last, weekday of a month, the way many holidays and meetings are set.
- [Weekdays & week numbers](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/weekdays-and-week-numbers/): the day of the week, the month, or the ISO week number a date falls in.
- [Age](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/age/): whole years from a birth date, today or on a day you name.
- [Date differences](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/date-differences/): the span between two dates, or the time until or since one. A count from today includes the part of today already gone, which is why it is not a whole number at noon, unless the app starts relative days at midnight.
- [Timestamps](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/timestamps/): a Unix timestamp, a count of seconds since 1970, read as the date it names, and a date written as one.
- [Working days](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/working-days/): counting only the days that are not weekends (nor public holidays, when the host application supplies them).
- [Displaying dates](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/displaying-dates/): whether a date is spelled out or written in numbers is a setting in the host application, not something a line writes. A date before year 1 is written with its era.
- [Time](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/time/): clock times, durations, and the span between two times, with frame rates and timecode. A clock time is shown as the time of day, with the days it has moved beside it when it crosses midnight.
- [Time zones](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/time-zones/): a time in another place, in several places at once, and the office hours two places share. Without a date the answer is today's; add `on 23 September 2026` to fix the day, since clocks change through the year.
- [Timesheets](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/timesheets/): adding up hours worked from clock times or spans, and paying them at an hourly rate.

## Units

- [Unit arithmetic](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/unit-arithmetic/): quantities in different units add and subtract, with the answer in the first one's unit.
- [Multiplying and dividing units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/unit-algebra/): units multiply, divide and cancel the way numbers do, so an area comes out in square metres and a price per kilogram times a weight comes out in money.
- [Cooking](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/cooking/): oven gas marks, the US, metric and imperial cups, and the number to multiply a recipe by when it has to serve a different number of people.
- [Converting units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/converting-units/): a quantity turned into another unit with `to`, `in` or `into`.
- [Other representations](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/unit-representations/): `as` shows a value in another form, such as a percentage or an exact fraction.
- [Defining your own units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/custom-units/): a unit the engine does not ship, named in terms of one it does.
- [CSS units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/css-units/): pixels and rems (a size relative to the page's base font size) for front-end work, at the usual 16px base or one you name.
- [Screen and image sizes](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/screen-and-image-sizes/): the shape of a screen or an image (its aspect ratio), the other side after a resize, and how large it prints at a stated density.
- [Rates & speeds](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/rates-and-speeds/): units written with a slash, such as km/h, converted like any other and multiplied or divided back into distance and time.
- [Travel](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/travel/): what a journey burns in fuel, what it costs, and how long it takes.
- [Fuel economy](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/fuel-economy/): miles per gallon (US or imperial) and litres per 100 km, which run opposite ways (more miles per gallon is fewer litres per 100 km).
- [Named derived units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/derived-units/): quantities multiplied into a named physical unit, such as volts times amps into watts.
- [Electricity](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/electricity/): volts, amps, ohms and amp-hours, with Ohm's law, and the energy a battery holds.
- [Energy units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/energy-units/): calories and kilocalories, BTU, therms and electronvolts, beside joules and kilowatt-hours.
- [Pressure](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/pressure/): pascals, bar, psi, atmospheres and millimetres of mercury, from tyres to blood pressure.
- [Distances in space](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/distances-in-space/): the astronomical unit, the light-year and the parsec.
- [Moles](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/moles/): the mole and the millimole, chemistry's count of particles.
- [Surveying & older units](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/surveying-units/): furlongs, chains, rods and other historic units of length and mass.
- [Geometry](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/geometry/): the area, perimeter and volume of the common shapes, from their dimensions.
- [Health & fitness](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/health/): body mass index (BMI, a weight measured against a height), and the pace or speed of a run from its distance and time.

## Text

- [Text operations](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/text-operations/): text in quotes, measured, tested and reshaped: its length, its case, and what it contains.
- [Pasted text](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/pasted-text/): the numbers, the amounts of money or one field of JSON pulled out of text pasted from a receipt, a log or an API response.
- [Text encoding](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/text-encoding/): text turned into base64, a URL-safe form or hex bytes and back again, which is how text travels through systems that accept only certain characters.
- [Hashing](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/hashing/): the digest of a piece of text, a short fingerprint that changes completely when one character changes, used to check that data arrived intact.
- [Networking](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/networking/): IPv4 and IPv6 subnets, the blocks of addresses a network is divided into: how many machines (hosts) one holds, its netmask, first and last address, and whether an address falls inside it. An IPv6 address is shown in its agreed short form.

## Visual

- [Charts](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/charts/): a series or a function turned into a chart. The engine never draws: it describes the chart as data, and the host application draws it.
- [Colours](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/colours/): hex, rgb, hsl and named colours as values, with functions to lighten, mix and check the contrast between them.

## Everyday

- [Coordinates, distance and bearing](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/coordinates/): places on the globe by latitude and longitude, and the distance and compass direction between two of them.
- [Dice](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/dice/): a random whole number in a range. `random seed` makes the draws repeat, which is how this one can be checked.
- [Randomness](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/random/): random identifiers and choices: a uuid, random hex, a pick from a list, a shuffle and a coin toss, repeatable after a seed.

## Live data

- [Weather](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/weather/): the current conditions and temperature for a place, as in `weather in London`, from a free service that needs no key. The answer is live, so it is named here rather than checked.
- [Knowledge](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/knowledge/): a plain-English question, as in `ask: distance to the moon`, handed to an answering function the host application supplies. The answer comes from that function, so it is named here rather than checked.
- [Frozen answers](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/frozen-answers/): `frozen` keeps a line's answer fixed, with the day it was fixed, so a live rate in a shared note reads the same later. It is shown on a plain sum here, since a live rate has no fixed answer to check.

## Working across lines

- [Variables](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/variables/): a name for a value, to use it again later, written with or without a leading colon, and of one word or a few (`hourly rate = $50`). `+=` and `-=` keep a running total, and a function of your own is defined the same way.
- [Line references](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/line-references/): an earlier line read by its number or its position, and the lines above totalled, by `total above` or by a line that is only `sum` or `total`.
- [Category tags](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/category-tags/): a `#tag` in the middle of a line labels its category and is left out of that line's own answer. `total of`, `average of` and `count of` gather every line carrying the tag, and `total by tag` breaks the whole note down. A tag starts with a letter, which keeps it clear of a colour such as `#c0ffee`.
- [Sections](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/sections/): the lines under a markdown heading, down to the next heading at the same level or above, are its section, added up by the heading's name from anywhere below it.
- [Table columns](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/table-columns/): a markdown table's column totalled or averaged by its name, and one cell read by the label on its row, the way you read a price off a list.
- [table lookups](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/table-lookups/): a markdown table's column totalled or averaged by its name, and one cell read by the label on its row, the way you read a price off a list.
- [Banded rates](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/banded-rates/): a tax, commission or tariff schedule written as a table of bands, where each rate applies only to the part of the amount inside its band.
- [Checks](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/checks/): `check` and a comparison, a line stating something the note should keep true, with a margin written `≈ ... within`.
- [Goal seek](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/goal-seek/): working backwards to the input that makes a line reach a target you name.
- [Tracing inputs](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/tracing-inputs/): which lines fed a result, and which lines fed those.
- [Trigger words](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/trigger-words/): ordinary words such as `total` and `sum` are not reserved keywords, so a variable can take one as its name.
- [What-if and sweeps](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/what-if/): what a line would say if an input were different, without editing the note, or its answers across a range of inputs.

## Embedding

- [Quick start](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/getting-started/quick-start/): installing the package, evaluating a line and formatting its value.
- [Entry points](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/guide/entry-points/): which call evaluates a single line and which a whole document.
- [TypeScript usage](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/guide/typescript-usage/): the value a line returns, and its failures.
- [Formatting](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/guide/formatting/): turning a value into display text.
- [Cheatsheet](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/syntax/cheatsheet/): one proven line for each area above.

## Optional

- [Every proven example](https://liamriddell.github.io/solve-engine/llms-full.txt): each example from the syntax pages with the answer the engine gives.
